saml.description: If the SAML Identity Provider Entity ID is empty, Keycloak does not validate the Issuer of received SAML assertions.
saml.note: A forged assertion with an unexpected Issuer may be accepted by design unless issuer validation is explicitly configured.

saml.description: On first brokered login, Keycloak may create a new local user, prompt to link an existing account, or require re-authentication depending on the configured First Login Flow.
saml.note: Identity merges or prompts during first login are often flow-driven behavior, not principal-binding vulnerabilities.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the external identity provider and may mark them verified.
saml.note: Email-based linking outcomes differ significantly when this switch is enabled; tests must account for it.

saml.description: If Case-sensitive username is disabled, the username from the identity provider is lower-cased when federating users.
saml.note: Case-only differences may collapse by design and should not be reported as unexpected identity collisions.

saml.description: When Trust Email is enabled, brokered email addresses are treated as verified and may be updated on subsequent logins with sync mode FORCE.
saml.note: Email-based linking or verified-email state changes may be configured behavior, not a vulnerability.

saml.description: Automatically Set Existing User in first broker login links existing users without verification.
saml.note: This can look like account takeover but is explicitly documented as dangerous configuration, not an implementation bug.

saml.description: TOTP codes are not remembered and can be reused within the valid time interval unless reusable-code policy forbids reuse semantics at the authenticator level.
saml.note: Replay of a TOTP within its validity window is documented behavior and not evidence of session replay weakness in SAML brokering.

saml.description: For SAML step-up authentication, Keycloak returns the legacy unspecified AuthnContextClassRef instead of an error when the feature is disabled or mappings/mappers are absent.
saml.note: Missing requested AuthnContext enforcement may be backward-compatibility behavior unless step-up-authentication-saml and mappings are configured.

saml.description: If an identity provider is unlinked from an organization, existing organization group mappings are preserved but no longer active; authentication still succeeds.
saml.note: Missing organization-group assignment after unlink is by design and should not be treated as inconsistent authorization enforcement.

saml.description: First broker login flow may create a new local user, link to an existing account, or require re-authentication/email verification depending on configured authenticators.
saml.note: Unexpected account creation or linking prompts are often flow-driven, not security bugs.

saml.constraint: For SAML issuer-validation tests (I1 saml_issuer_mismatch), create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST set identity_provider_entity_id (config.idpEntityId). If this field is empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation on received SAML assertions.

For SAML signature-validation default tests (I1 saml_cert_substitution), create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST leave validate_signature and want_assertions_signed unset or OFF when testing insecure defaults. If validate_signature is ON and proper validating certificates are configured, attacker-signed assertions should be rejected by design.

For positive-control SAML signature tests, if use_metadata_descriptor_url is OFF then validating_x509_certificates (config.signingCertificate) MUST contain the trusted IdP certificate(s). Otherwise signature validation cannot succeed even for valid assertions.

For I1 assertion-signature integrity tests, want_assertions_signed controls whether Keycloak expects a signed Assertion. A response-level signature alone may be insufficient when this is enabled. To test acceptance of unsigned assertions or envelope-only signatures, vary want_assertions_signed explicitly and interpret success/failure relative to that setting.

For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, do NOT assume Service Provider Entity ID enforces issuer validation. service_provider_entity_id identifies Keycloak to the remote IdP; issuer checking of inbound assertions is controlled by identity_provider_entity_id only.

For I2 SAML replay and expiry tests, include a CONTROL brokered login with a valid assertion before the attack login. Without a control, a failed SAML login may reflect broken provider setup, first-login flow friction, or missing certificates rather than freshness enforcement.

For I2 SAML assertion expiry tests, Keycloak authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, which is 30 minutes by default. The executor must complete the SP-initiated flow and POST the forged SAMLResponse before the authentication session expires, or the result may be an expired authentication session rather than assertion-time validation.

For I3 config-change tests, new brokered logins are evaluated against the current identity provider configuration by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same login flow before and after admin reconfiguration, not treat legitimate config updates as inconsistencies.

Principal matching semantics: principal_type selects either Subject NameID or a SAML attribute as the external identifier; principal_attribute is an exact attribute name/friendly-name selector, not a wildcard or regex matcher. For I4 multi-identity tests, do NOT set principal_attribute to '*' expecting broad matching; omit or choose the exact attribute actually present in the assertion.

General IDP essential-claim matching semantics: Essential claim value supports regular expression format when Verify essential claim is enabled. If this filter is configured, multi-identity I4 tests must ensure every tested identity satisfies the regex; otherwise omit the filter entirely. Do not confuse regex support here with exact-only matching used by other fields such as principal_attribute.

Case behavior for brokered usernames: if Case-sensitive username is disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating users, although server usernames are always lower-case. I4 case-confusion tests must account for this normalization and should inspect granted identity rather than assuming original case is preserved.

For I4 account-linking and collision tests, First Login Flow materially changes behavior. The default first broker login flow may create a new user if unique, or prompt/link based on matching email/username. Tests for identity collapse must control firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias and trust_email settings, otherwise merges or prompts may be by-design flow behavior rather than a broker flaw.

For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, Trust Email MUST be considered. When trust_email is ON, Keycloak trusts email addresses from the identity provider and may mark them verified on first federation and on subsequent logins with sync mode FORCE. Auto-linking conclusions are invalid unless trust_email is explicitly set to the intended value.

For I4 organization-linked IdP tests, an identity provider can be linked to only a single organization, and organization-specific group mappings become inactive if the IdP is unlinked. Do not interpret missing organization group assignment after unlink as an authorization bug; authentication continues successfully by design.

For I5 authorization-binding tests involving roles in issued tokens/assertions, Keycloak includes only the intersection of user-assigned roles and the client's role scope mappings. Missing roles may be caused by client scope configuration rather than broker claim loss; configure client scopes and Full Scope Allowed consistently before testing escalation or suppression.

For I5 scope/downscoping tests on Keycloak-issued tokens after SAML brokering, optional client scopes are only applied when requested, while default client scopes are always applied. The fuzzer must distinguish default-scope claims from requested-scope claims before flagging over-grant.

For I5 organization claim tests, requesting scope=organization maps a single organization if the user belongs to one organization, may prompt for selection if the user belongs to multiple organizations, and organization:* maps all organizations. Multi-org results are by design and must not be treated as overbroad authorization without considering the requested organization scope format.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, organization groups and realm groups are distinct. Organization groups cannot be used in Keycloak authorization policies; only realm groups are supported there. Do not flag absence of organization-group-based policy enforcement as a bug in the authorization engine.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy Hashing iterations uses -1 as a sentinel meaning use the algorithm default iteration count (argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never assume -1 disables hashing or means literal negative iterations.

Numeric sentinel: Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses 0 as a sentinel meaning the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password. Do not interpret 0 as 'use default' or 'disable re-authentication'.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn timeout uses 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation, not a literal zero-second timeout. Tests must not assume immediate expiry when timeout=0.
Numeric sentinel: User session count limiter uses 0 to disable the realm or client session-count check, not to enforce zero sessions. Do not treat 0 as deny-all.

Numeric sentinel: Client secret rotation uses Rotated Secret Expiration=0 to remove the old secret immediately during rotation. This is not 'use default'; it means no overlap window for the previous secret.

Numeric sentinel: Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 if not configured. When the limit is reached, the oldest authentication sub-session is removed as new ones are created. High-concurrency browser tests can evict older auth sub-sessions rather than fail explicitly.

For SAML broker testing of I1 signature validation, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and config.wantAssertionsSigned=true when testing secure configurations. The documentation states Validate Signature controls whether requests/responses from the external IDP are expected to be digitally signed, and Want Assertions Signed controls whether the SP expects a signed Assertion. If omitted or left OFF, successful forged SAMLResponse logins may be by configuration rather than a vulnerability.

For insecure-default I1 tests, a separate baseline MUST create the SAML IdP with default config and without config.validateSignature=true or config.wantAssertionsSigned=true. The docs indicate these are configurable toggles rather than guaranteed defaults. A login success in this mode only demonstrates insecure or permissive configuration/defaults, not bypass of an explicitly enabled validation check.

Identity Provider Entity ID matching is EXACT string match only. The documentation says this field is used to validate the Issuer for received SAML assertions and if empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do NOT set this field to wildcard-like values; omit it entirely only when intentionally testing missing issuer validation. Setting a wildcard string will be treated literally, not as pattern matching.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure config.identity_provider_entity_id explicitly on the SAML IdP. If this field is empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation by design, so an accepted wrong issuer is not evidence of issuer-mismatch bypass under configured trust.

Principal Type/Principal Attribute determine which assertion field identifies the external user. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST control whether identity is derived from Subject NameID or a SAML attribute. If Principal Type is set to a SAML attribute, NameID mutations alone may not affect downstream identity binding and can produce false negatives.

Case-sensitive username is a broker setting that changes how federated usernames are stored. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating users, while server usernames are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST record whether caseSensitiveOriginalUsername is enabled; Admin vs admin collapsing may be by design when disabled.

Trust Email marks brokered emails as verified when enabled, and subsequent logins can update this under sync mode FORCE. For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST set trustEmail=false on the provider or otherwise treat email-verified linking as configured behavior. Testing takeover via unverified email while trustEmail=true can misattribute configured trust to a vulnerability.

First Login Flow materially affects account linking and user creation. The default first broker login flow may create a new user if unique, or prompt/link existing accounts by email verification or re-authentication. For I4 account-collision and linking tests, the fuzzer MUST pin the firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias and interpret outcomes in light of that flow; automatic linking or blocking may be by configured flow design.

The AutoLink/Automatically Set Existing User first-login configuration is documented as dangerous and links existing users without verification. If a test realm uses such a flow, identity merges based on email/username are BY DESIGN and MUST NOT be reported as a broker flaw without noting the configured authenticator choice.

Post login flow can enforce additional authentication such as OTP after broker login. For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, a valid test MUST compare the same user with and without SAML under a realm where the relevant post-login flow is actually bound to the SAML provider. If post login flow is unset, missing MFA after SAML may be expected configuration rather than bypass.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default per documentation. SAML broker flows are session-bound; the executor must initiate the SP flow and submit the forged SAMLResponse before the authentication session expires, or failures may be due to expired auth session rather than security enforcement.

Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other browser tabs using the same browser session. For I3 flow-coherence tests involving multiple concurrent browser tabs or repeated SP-initiated flows, the fuzzer MUST isolate browser state per sequence to avoid automatic reauthentication masking session-binding issues.

SAML POST binding is recommended and the broker endpoint consumes POSTed form data. The saml_login operation MUST use POST form submission with SAMLResponse and RelayState and MUST initiate the SAML flow first so InResponseTo matches the outstanding AuthnRequest. Sending an unsolicited fabricated response without flow initiation will be rejected for protocol reasons, not security reasons.

For I1 tests distinguishing response-signature vs assertion-signature validation, Want Assertions Signed must be considered separately from Validate Signature. A configuration that validates signed responses but does not require signed assertions may accept envelope-only signatures by design. The fuzzer MUST test both toggles explicitly and not assume one implies the other.

For I5 audience tests on SAML clients, Assertion Lifespan and SAML Conditions are client-side/SP-side concepts for issued assertions, while brokered SAML login validation depends on the incoming assertion Conditions and AudienceRestriction. A successful login with missing Conditions or wrong Audience should only be flagged when the incoming assertion was accepted by the brokered IdP flow, not confused with client issuance settings.

Requested AuthnContext comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better. For step-up or MFA-related SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST account for comparison semantics; a different but stronger context may satisfy a request under non-Exact modes, so acceptance is not necessarily an authorization-binding failure.

When step-up-authentication-saml is not enabled, or no URI/LoA mapping exists, or the AuthnContextClassRef mapper is not executed, Keycloak returns the unspecified AuthnContext by design instead of enforcing requested contexts. Tests expecting NoAuthnContext or strict AuthnContext enforcement MUST verify the feature and mappings are configured first.

For SAML client redirect URI handling, Valid Redirect URIs allow wildcards only at the end of a URL. If the Assertion Consumer URL is taken from the request, it must match a registered pattern. Access or login failures caused by redirect URI mismatch are setup errors, not security rejections.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 to disable the check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions. If configured, Deny new session or Terminate oldest session outcomes are by design and can affect repeated login sequences.

The authenticationSessions SPI authSessionsLimit numeric parameter uses a default of 300 authentication sub-sessions per root authentication session; when the limit is reached, the oldest sub-session is removed. This is not a token-use budget, but high-concurrency browser-flow tests may evict older pending SAML auth sub-sessions and cause protocol failures unrelated to invariants.

For OIDC-based verification after SAML brokering, session_token MUST be the access_token from the token endpoint or direct grant, not an ID token. UserInfo and broker token retrieval endpoints require a bearer access token.

For SAML signature-validation tests (I1 saml_cert_substitution, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST explicitly set config.validateSignature=true and, when testing assertion signatures, config.wantAssertionsSigned=true. Documentation describes these as toggles; leaving them unset/OFF can cause acceptance of unsigned or differently signed content by configuration, not by vulnerability.

For default-config insecurity checks, the fuzzer MAY intentionally omit config.validateSignature and config.wantAssertionsSigned when creating the SAML IdP. If forged SAML login then succeeds, report as insecure default only, not as bypass of an explicitly enabled control.

Principal selection for brokered SAML identities is controlled by config.principalType and config.principalAttribute. For I4 identity-collision tests, the fuzzer MUST hold these constant across compared logins. Changing principal source between Subject NameID and SAML attribute changes the identity key by design and invalidates collision conclusions.

If config.principalType uses a SAML attribute, config.principalAttribute is an EXACT attribute-name/friendly-name selector; the documentation provides no wildcard or regex companion mode. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, do NOT set a wildcard-like value expecting broad match semantics; use the exact attribute name or omit attribute-based principal selection.

Subject NameID cannot be used together with NameID Policy Format urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient. When testing I4 NameID-based identity binding, do not configure transient NameID format with principalType=SUBJECT. This combination is invalid by design and can cause setup failures unrelated to security.

For I2 replay tests against SAML, include a CONTROL brokered login first using the same provider configuration but without the replay mutation. Without a successful control, a failed replay attempt cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup or first-login-flow friction.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion and other freshness tests, include a CONTROL login with a valid assertion before the mutated expired assertion. Otherwise, rejection may be caused by unrelated broker configuration, first login flow, or missing user-linking prerequisites.

Keycloak first-broker-login behavior can create, link, or challenge on existing accounts depending on First Login Flow and Post Login Flow. For I4 account-linking and collision tests, the fuzzer MUST keep firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias/postBrokerLoginFlowAlias fixed and interpret linking outcomes in light of that flow. Auto-linking or re-authentication prompts can be by-design.

Trust Email marks brokered email as verified when enabled, and with sync mode FORCE this can be updated on subsequent logins. For I4 unverified_email_account_linking tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST set trustEmail=false. Otherwise, email-based linking/verification behavior may be by configuration rather than a vulnerability.

Case-sensitive username is configurable for identity providers. If disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased before federation. For I4 case_confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST record whether case-sensitive username is enabled. Admin vs admin collapsing is by design when case sensitivity is disabled.

Organization-linked identity providers can auto-redirect based on email domain and can add users to organization groups during first broker login. For I4/I5 tests in realms with organizations enabled, the fuzzer MUST avoid organization-linked IdPs unless the test explicitly targets organization behavior, because organization context changes login flow and group assignment by design.

SAML POST binding is the recommended and documented secure binding because Redirect binding exposes SAML responses in URLs. The saml_login operation MUST use POST with form-encoded SAMLResponse and RelayState, and metadata.initiate_saml_flow=true so the executor obtains a matching AuthnRequest/InResponseTo.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. SAML multi-step flows are session-bound. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST complete SP-initiated flow initiation and forged response submission within the same live authentication session; otherwise failures are due to expired auth session, not coherence bugs.

Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other browser tabs after one tab completes login because authentication sub-sessions share a root authentication session. For I3 tests, do not interpret cross-tab restarts or resumed logins as session confusion unless the same request is inconsistently evaluated within one intended flow.

The authenticationSessions SPI parameter authSessionsLimit has sentinel semantics: value 300 is the documented default maximum number of AuthenticationSessionEntity per RootAuthenticationSessionEntity; when the limit is reached, the oldest sub-session is removed on new authentication requests. Do not assume unlimited parallel auth sub-sessions.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0=disabled for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions. If testing session-limit interactions, set a positive value explicitly.
Password policy Maximum Authentication Age uses sentinel 0=always re-authenticate before password update. Do not interpret 0 as 'no limit'.
Password policy Hashing iterations uses sentinel -1=use algorithm default iterations, not disable hashing or zero iterations. Exact defaults depend on selected algorithm.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
